segments.expected: "I'm sure of my reading," said the Proprietor. "I've been sure of it for seventy-six years. I'm not certain I'm right." He said it quite simply, as he might have said the time. "Those are two different things, sir. I've been a clerk. I know the difference between a count and what it means." He turned his head and looked down the table at Kiva again. "Which is why I asked the Board to bring Miss Rowan. I'd like to ask her one question. Through the Board, if the Board allows it. She's not obliged to answer." The Clerk looked at Kiva. "You're not obliged," she said.
